Given that $m∠A<{90}^{∘},$ calculate $m∠A.$ Round the answer to the nearest degree.
question.worked_solution:
The Law of Sines states that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡A}{a}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡B}{b}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
a=20,\,m∠B={35}^{∘},\,b=12,
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡A}{20} & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{35}^{∘}}{12} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =20\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{35}^{∘}}{12} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{35}^{∘}}{3} \\  & ≈\frac{5\cdot 0.574}{3} \\  & ≈0.957,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to five decimal places.

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A & ≈\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.957)≈{73}^{∘},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest degree.
